To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the striatum is a critical brain structure for the acquisition and automatization of higher‐order sequential knowledge; (2) this knowledge is acquired through the interaction of prefrontal cortex and caudate nucleus networks; and (3) the striatum contributes to the selection of the optimal response by integrating both the current and past stimuli.
the striatum plays a significant role not only in the implicit acquisition, but also in the implicit processing, of sequential knowledge in the serial reaction time task.

the striatum, in addition to the prefrontal cortex, is a critical brain area for implicit sequence learning and that it is involved in more complex sequential knowledge processing than simple pairwise associations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the acquisition of sequential knowledge, its representation in the brain and its functional role.
the acquisition, retention and processing of sequential knowledge.
the neural basis of sequence learning and the acquisition of sequential knowledge.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

striatum is involved with the implicit acquisition of statistical knowledge, and is also involved with the implicit selection and preparation of appropriate responses, both processes contributing to the automatization of sequential knowledge in the SRT‐task.

the caudate nucleus and the putamen are involved in both the acquisition of statistical knowledge (i.e., the implicit acquisition of the grammar) and in its subsequent application (i.e., implicit sequence processing), while the ventral putamen seems to be specifically involved in implicit sequence learning.
the caudate nucleus is involved in the acquisition and automatization of sequential information through the implicit acquisition of statistical regularities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
striatum is involved not only in implicit sequence learning, but also in higher‐order sequential knowledge processing.
we have demonstrated that the striatum plays a significant role in implicit learning, and that this role is not limited to simple associations, but also includes more complex sequential knowledge.
the striatum plays an important role in the implicit processing and automatization of sequential information.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the striatum has a role in more than simple associations.

the striatum plays an essential role in the processing of higher‐order knowledge, and that the striatum has the capacity to integrate information from the previous trials in the context of the current trial.
the striatum has the capacity to learn and process higher‐order sequential knowledge.
